dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows who something belongs to — the author of a post, the people in a conversation, the owner of a task — by a small picture, and still has something to show when a person has no picture or the picture does not arrive: their initials, or a glyph. It shows a person small beside a line of text, at a row's height in a list, and large at the top of that person's page; it tells a person from a team or a project by the box's shape; and it shows several people as one stack that says how many more there are.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything an avatar reads: per size, the side of its box, the text style of its initials, the size of its fallback glyph and how far the avatars of a group overlap; per shape, the box's corners; the quiet fill behind a fallback and a loading picture; the color of the initials and of the glyph; and the gap a group draws around each of its avatars.
rules: An avatar stands for a person, or for a team, a project or another thing people act as. It is a picture, not a control: it takes no press and no focus and has no states. An avatar that goes somewhere or opens something is placed inside a link or a Button, which draws the states.
Give label the name it stands for. Beside a visible name set decorative, so the name is not read twice; alone, the label is its accessible name.
The avatar does not make initials from a name: writing systems and naming orders differ. The product gives initials; with neither a picture nor initials a glyph is drawn.
Every fallback has the same quiet fill and content color. Do not color avatars per person: a color that means nothing is not in the system.
A circle is a person; a square is something that is not one person (a team, a project, an organisation, a bot).
A dot or a count on an avatar is a badge wrapped around it, and means what a badge means everywhere: something is waiting.
Several avatars shown as one stack are a group: the group gives the size and the shape, and counts the ones it does not draw.
container.size is the box's exact side, not a minimum: an avatar does not grow with enlarged text, as a glyph's box does not.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a round picture or a monogram by hand.

size.$description: The side of the avatar's square box, per size. Small stands beside one line of text (a byline, a table cell) and is the size a chip gives an avatar; medium is the size a list row gives a leading avatar; large heads a person's own page or card and is the size a list row gives a leading image. An exact side, not a minimum.

shape.$description: The box's corners, per shape, never larger than half its side. What the picture is clipped to.

color.$description: The fill behind the initials, behind the glyph, behind a picture that is still loading and behind the transparent parts of a picture: the quiet tone a list row puts behind its leading avatar. The same for every person.

typescale.$description: The text style of the initials, per size: a label style small enough for two letters to stand in the box with room at their sides.

color.$description: The color of the initials and of a group's count: secondary content on the quiet fill.

size.$description: The box of the fallback glyph, per size: a step of the icon scale that leaves the glyph a clear margin inside the avatar.

color.$description: The color of the fallback glyph: the initials' color.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows the people of one thing — the reviewers of a change, the members of a channel, the authors of a page — in the room of two or three avatars, and says how many more there are.

overlap.$description: How far each avatar of a group lies over the one before it, per size: a quarter of the box's side in the default system, so three quarters of every face stays in view.

width.$description: The width of the gap a group draws around each of its avatars, outside the avatar's edge, so two pictures that overlap are read as two.

color.$description: The color of that gap: the surface the group sits on, as a badge's outline is. A product that places a group on another surface sets that surface's color here for that place.
